solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deficiency of blood sugar approaching danger level? That's false

parts.note: a hypo is the everyday short name for hypoglycaemia, low blood sugar
critical describes a condition close to the danger point

explanation.surface: A diabetic's low blood sugar is nearing danger, then someone declares the alarm a falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'That's false' look like a reply to the scare; 'That's' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-faced person professes beliefs they do not hold, so their professions are insincere and untrue.

clue.text: Foreign city hospital getting exposed in time after being built up

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: built up in a down clue means written from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards
in places the exposed word inside the time word

parts.note: a day is a period of time
bared means exposed

explanation.surface: A hospital abroad is uncovered during construction work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'built up' means written upwards, so 'after being built up' reverses the whole container to YDERABAD; 'in' does the containing first.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of the Indian state of Telangana is a city outside Britain, one of India's largest.

clue.text: With no hesitation indulge a beast of symbolic significance

indicators.note: with no means without, so the hesitation sound is dropped from the verb

parts.note: to pander is to indulge someone's wishes
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Without a second thought, someone indulges a creature that stands for something larger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' removes ER from PANDER; A is the clue's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bear is the logo of the World Wildlife Fund and a symbol of China, an animal with emblematic meaning.

clue.text: Plants needing minimal cold protected by man on island

indicators.note: protected by means shielded all round, so the cold letter sits inside

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a man
C is the shortest form of cold, its abbreviation on a tap

explanation.surface: Some plants that need almost no cold are sheltered by a man on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT is a hip jazz-age word for a man; 'protected by' puts C inside CAT, and I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents with spines are a familiar family of plants.

clue.text: Home building material — builder finally brought in a bit more

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: brought in means carried inside, so the builder's letter goes into the material

parts.note: cement is a building material

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of builder

explanation.surface: A house-builder brings in a little more material for a home extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from builder, and 'brought in' places it inside CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small step up in quantity, such as a pay rise, is an increase, a little extra.

clue.text: Swell cuties — men getting jittery

indicators.note: jittery means agitated and twitching, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Pretty young things and the men around them grow nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like slang praise for the cuties, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical verb for becoming swollen or puffed up, as tissue does, means to swell.

clue.text: Strange story featured in a newspaper's leader

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so the story sits within the other letters
leader picks the first letter of newspaper's

parts.note: a story can mean a lie, as in telling stories

explanation.surface: An odd tale appears in a paper's editorial column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like the editorial, but it picks N; 'featured in' puts LIE between A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreign and unfamiliar, outside one's experience, is strange.

clue.text: It's coming from above, using divine portal possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something descends from heaven, perhaps through a holy gateway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' only links; the divine portal makes the definition's heavenly sense apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Help that arrives by the care of God is described as sent by heaven, coming from on high.

clue.text: One to show man embracing woman

definitions.text: One to show man embracing woman

indicators.note: a man embracing someone holds them in his arms, so one name wraps round the other

parts.note: Ron is a short man's name
Di is a short woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone whose job is to depict a man hugging a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the French sculptor's best-known work, The Kiss, shows exactly a man embracing a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The French sculptor exhibited The Kiss, a marble pair of lovers locked together, so he is one who displays such an embrace.

clue.text: Not half unwell in bed, is ill on account of drinks

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: not half tells us to drop half of the word for unwell, keeping its back two letters

parts.note: sick means unwell
ails means is ill

explanation.surface: Someone is laid up in bed, very poorly, and blames it on the drinks they had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps the back half, CK, which 'in' sets inside the bed; 'unwell in bed' reads as one idea but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed alcoholic beverages served at a party are a familiar kind of drink.

clue.text: Instruction for making a ledge taking up a lot of room?

definitions.text: taking up a lot of room?

parts.note: the second word spread out, its letters rearranged, gives a ledge

explanation.surface: Directions for building a shelf that turns out to be enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: SPREAD means rearrange EAGLED, which gives A LEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sprawled with arms and legs stretched wide, like a heraldic eagle, occupies plenty of space.

clue.text: What's very bad about substitute not quite able to play in any position?

definitions.text: able to play in any position

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the bad word goes round the cut-down substitute

parts.note: vile describes something very bad

indicators.note: not quite tells us to leave off the last letter of the word for substitute

parts.note: ersatz means a substitute or imitation

explanation.surface: A manager grumbles about a substitute player who cannot quite fill every position on the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substitute' looks like the football sense but is the German loanword for an imitation; 'not quite' leaves ERSAT and 'about' wraps the bad word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A player with many skills who can fill any role on the team is called adaptable or all-round.

clue.text: Soldier leading his colleagues in historic district

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the soldier goes in front of his colleagues

parts.note: a man is a soldier, as in officers and men
OR stands for other ranks, the soldier's fellow non-officers

explanation.surface: A soldier marches ahead of his comrades through an old quarter of town.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the army term for the soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of a medieval lord formed an estate, and the word is also slang for a police officer's patch.

clue.text: It's problematical when article is wedged between back-to-back items of furniture

indicators.note: wedged between means squeezed into the gap separating the two pieces

parts.note: a bed turned round to sit back to back with a table, giving DEB then TABLE
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Squeezing something between two pieces of furniture placed back to back causes difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-back' turns the first item round so the two pieces meet back to back, and 'is wedged between' puts the article in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to question and argument, with no clear answer, is problematical.

clue.text: Surprisingly, artier mother embraces the ultimate unknown poetic style

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the unknown goes inside
surprisingly signals that the letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, and z is the last of them

explanation.surface: A rather arty mother takes up a mysterious form of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' gives TERARI, and 'embraces' takes Z inside; algebra's unknowns run x, y, z, so z is the ultimate one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's interlocking three-line rhyme scheme, used in the Divine Comedy, is an Italian verse form.

clue.text: Writer of song with no commercial value

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the advert is removed from the song

parts.note: a ballad is a song
an ad is a commercial
point can mean value or use, as in what's the point

explanation.surface: A songwriter's work has no money-making potential.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface ties 'commercial value' together, but they split; 'with no' leaves BALL, and 'Writer' means a pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen with a small rolling sphere at its tip is an instrument used for writing.

clue.text: Part protected by water barriers

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded by, so the abbreviation sits inside the water

parts.note: the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: A section of coast is shielded by sea defences.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'water barriers' as one phrase, but 'water' gives SEA and 'barriers' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy and botany, partitions dividing cavities, like the wall inside the nose, are dividing walls.

clue.text: Quickly losing love, this person's held to be important

indicators.note: held means gripped inside, so the possessive sits in the shortened word
losing means giving up, so the love letter is dropped

parts.note: pronto means quickly
O is love, a zero score in tennis
mine means belonging to this person, the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone who quickly loses a lover insists that what they have counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' leaves PRONT, and 'held' wraps it round the possessive; love is O from the zero score in tennis, and 'to be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing out and well known, like a leading figure, means being significant.

clue.text: One found guilty of fraud — how low can you get?

definitions.meaning: Asil ..., the Polly Peck tycoon convicted in 2012 of stealing from his company
the lowest point of anything, the bottom of a decline

explanation.surface: A fraudster's conviction prompts the scornful question of how far a person can sink.
explanation.walkthrough: Asil Nadir ran the Polly Peck company, which collapsed in 1990; he fled to Northern Cyprus and was convicted on returning to Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The businessman is a convicted swindler, and the astronomical term for the point beneath the observer means the lowest point.

clue.text: Article in case stuck in tree, not stiff

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside, so the tree wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a lime is a tree, also called the linden
the is the definite article
so can mean provided that, standing in for in case

explanation.surface: Something in a case has got wedged up in a tree and refuses to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' puts the article and the short word for 'in case' inside the tree; the stuck object makes 'not stiff' a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and flexible, and the longer form means the same: moving easily, bending without rigidity.

clue.text: Roman below — when given grant such becomes not at all sweet

indicators.note: the clue says adding a word makes a longer one, so the short word is that longer one with the addition taken away

parts.note: in- plus fragrant reads as not fragrant, smelling the opposite of sweet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman down below gets a grant, which turns out to smell anything but sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' means Latin: the Latin word for below. Add GRANT and it becomes IN-FRAGRANT, read as not fragrant; 'such becomes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition meaning beneath, familiar from 'see infra' in footnotes, is a Roman word for below.

clue.text: Level of defeat

definitions.meaning: to knock down or baffle someone

explanation.surface: The extent of a defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is a level of a building, and to knock an opponent down or baffle them is to beat them.

clue.text: Annoying ringing sound around compound

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the sound wraps round the compound

parts.note: a ping is a short high ringing sound
an ester is a chemical compound

explanation.surface: A constant ringing noise from somewhere in the compound is getting on everyone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'compound' as an enclosed site, but here it is the chemical ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothering someone with repeated demands or noise is irritating them, which is what annoying means as a verb form.

clue.text: Indication to musicians to play last bit of the song

indicators.note: play signals the letters frolic into a new order
last bit of picks the final letter of the

explanation.surface: A note on the score tells the band to perform just the closing bars of the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last bit of' takes E from 'the', which is rearranged with SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for sign is the score mark showing performers where a repeat begins or ends.

clue.text: IT work

parts.note: a work in information technology form, read on a screen rather than printed

explanation.surface: A job in computing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a job in information technology, but 'work' is a written publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital publication read on a screen is a literary work produced by computer technology.

clue.text: Acclaiming return of number one Liberal, I celebrate

indicators.note: return means turning back, so number one is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician returns as party leader, and someone declares they will celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' is not a leader here but NO plus I, which 'return of' turns to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating someone as a celebrity and heaping praise on them is acclaiming them.

clue.text: Huge honour given to some that shouldn't get honour

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: shouldn't get means the honour is withheld, so it is taken out of the word some

parts.note: the OM, Order of Merit, is another British honour

explanation.surface: A big honour is handed to people who, in the speaker's view, don't deserve any honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that shouldn't get' takes the Order of Merit out of the clue's 'some', leaving SE; both honours are British awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone extremely overweight is very large, so the word stretches to mean enormous.

clue.text: There may be something in here that will have to be got off one's chest

definitions.text: There may be something in here that will have to be got off one's chest

parts.words: There may be something in here that will have to be got off one's chest
parts.note: to get something off one's chest is to confess a worry, but a pouch sewn on a jacket's chest literally holds things there

explanation.surface: Somewhere holds a secret that someone will need to confess.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for confessing is read literally: whatever is in this jacket pouch sits on the chest and must be taken off it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket pouch sewn over the chest holds items worn on the front of the upper body.
